changes.evidence: Gibbs, 383 U.S. at 724–726, addresses the restrictive approach developed after Hurn and states that discretion had consistently been recognized. Section 1367 supplies the statutory limits.

rule

A federal court with a substantial federal claim may also decide a non-federal ground for the same cause of action, even if the federal ground fails, but not a separate non-federal cause of action joined with it.

Under Hurn’s pre-Gibbs test, a court with a substantial federal claim could decide a non-federal ground for the same cause of action, even after the federal ground failed, but not a separate non-federal cause of action.
